other_considerations.note: The most common chest injury; a simple fracture could explain pain on inspiration and cough, can lead to pneumothorax, and is diagnosed with a CXR.

A major concern after trauma because of rapid blood loss; recent infectious mononucleosis raises the risk, and with left chest and left upper quadrant pain the spleen should be evaluated (ultrasound, then abdominal CT) and organomegaly looked for.
Causes severe pain that increases with inspiration or movement with an otherwise negative exam; may be simple viral pleuritis, but emergent causes must be ruled out first.

source_issues: p026: the surgery question ('Have you had any surgeries?') is answered 'No medications.' The note's PSH line also reads 'No medications.', so the note cannot resolve it; surgical history is unknown. Only the literal statement was recorded (added to the no-medications fact f044 with a flag).
The time of the accident is never stated; the pain and dyspnea began 'last night' (p001) and he 'felt okay at first'. The note does not give the time either.
p007 asks about mucus or blood in the cough; the answer describes yellow sputum and does not address blood.
The note's exam vitals (e002) give only temperature and respiratory rate; BP and HR come only from the doorway.
e003 (HEENT) contains 'no JVD', a neck finding.

e006: 'Soft, nondistended, @ BS x 4 quadrants' - '@' is a garbled symbol (probably '+', bowel sounds present); recorded as present with a flag (x013). The abdomen is not described as tender or nontender apart from LUQ tenderness.

e007 is a second 'HEENT' line ('No bruises or lacerations') placed after the abdomen; it may be a mislabeled skin exam (the checklist includes a skin inspection for abrasions, lacerations, bruising). The arm scratches the patient reports (p009) are not recorded anywhere in the exam.
Gold diagnoses #1 and #2 list 'RR 22/minute', a vital sign, under History Finding(s).
gold_additional_diagnosis (splenic rupture): 'in the chest area and LU the spleen' is truncated (probably 'LUQ,').
Name inconsistency: the opening gives 'John Matthew'; the sample closure says 'Mr. Matthews'.
Note HPI: 'unusual fluid from the mouth or nose' omits the ears asked about in p011.
notes: The opening fact has the stage direction '(holds chest, left side)' removed; it is kept in acting_notes, and the left-chest location is recorded in f004 with a flag. '(points to the LUQ)' in p019 is handled the same way (f024).
The cough 'for the past few days' (p006) may predate the accident (the pain began last night); recorded as stated with the patient's hedge 'I suppose'.

SP instructions that create observable signs are merged into the matching exam records: splinting on inspiration (x011), left chest tenderness (x010), LUQ tenderness (x013), fast shallow breaths (x005, with the note's 'dyspneic'); moaning and short answers are left as acting notes only.
Mother and father 'both healthy' is coded as an absent family-history item.
p012 asks 'Did you faint?' under the topic 'Loss of consciousness'; recorded as no fainting or loss of consciousness.

Conversion: the chief complaint gives two opening facts, trouble breathing (f001) and chest pain (f003). The onset 'last night' (p001) covers both and is a child of each (f002, f005), so either question gets an answer.

Conversion: the accident story (p003) is a parent 'car accident' (f009, v1 f005 + f006) with speed, car damage, seat belt and how he felt afterwards as children (v1 f007 split into speed and damage); not calling the police out of embarrassment (v1 f010, subtype other) is social_background (f054).

Conversion: v1 x030 ('Occasionally cough hard into a tissue', sp_notes) is not an exam record: coughing is pure behavior and the note's exam does not record it (CONVERSION.md); it stays in acting_notes.

Conversion: the sputum (p007) is an appearance child of the cough (f019); infectious mononucleosis is a parent (f042) with the illness 2 months ago as a child (f043); last meal (v1 subtype other) is habit_exposure.
